mn20:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Savatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapindika’s Park.
mn20:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn20:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is pursuing the Higher Mind, five signs can be given attention by him from time to time.
mn20:3.1: (i) ‘When, owing to some sign to which he is giving attention there arise in him evil, unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion, then some sign other than that sign and connected with what is profitable should be given attention by him.
mn20:3.2: When he gives attention to some sign other than that sign and connected with what is profitable, then any evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion, are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:3.3: With the abandoning of them his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:3.4: ‘Just as a skilled joiner or his apprentice might knock out, remove and extract a coarse peg by means of a fine one,
mn20:3.5: so too, when, owing to some sign ...
mn20:3.7: his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:4.1: (ii) ‘If, while he is giving attention to some sign other than that sign [first mentioned] and connected with what is profitable, there still arise in him evil, unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion, then the danger in those thoughts should be scrutinized by him thus:
mn20:4.2: “These thoughts are such that they are unprofitable, that they are reprehensible, that they result in suffering.”
mn20:4.3: When he scrutinizes the danger in those thoughts then any evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:4.4: With the abandoning of them his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:4.5: ‘Just as a woman—or a man—young, youthful and fond of ornaments would be horrified, humiliated and disgusted if a snake’s or a dog’s or a human being’s carcase, were hung round her neck,
mn20:4.6: so too, if, while he is giving attention …
mn20:4.9: his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:5.1: (iii) ‘If, when he is scrutinizing the danger in those thoughts, there still arise in him evil, unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion, then forgetting of those thoughts and non-attention to them should be tried.
mn20:5.2: When he tries forgetting those thoughts and non-attention to them then any evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:5.3: With the abandoning of them his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:5.4: ‘Just as a man with [good] eyes who did not want to see forms that had come within [the eyes’] range,
mn20:5.5: would either shut his eyes or look away,
mn20:5.6: so too, if, when he scrutinizes … his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:6.1: (iv) ‘If, when he tries forgetting those thoughts and non-attention to them, there still arise in him evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion, then settling of thought-formations should be given attention by him with respect to these thoughts.
mn20:6.2: When he gives attention to settling thought-formations with respect to those thoughts any evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:6.3: With the abandoning of them his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:6.21: for by doing so he would substitute for each grosser mode of deportment one that was subtler;
mn20:6.22: so too, if when he tries forgetting … his mind is settled in himself quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:7.1: (v) ‘If, while he is giving attention to settling of thought-formations with respect to those thoughts, there still arise in him evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion,
mn20:7.2: then with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth he should beat down, constrain and crush mind with mind.
mn20:7.3: When with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth, he beats down, constrains and crushes mind with mind, then any evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:7.4: With the abandoning of them his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:7.5: ‘Just as a strong man might seize a weaker one by the head or shoulders and beat him down, constrain and crush him,
mn20:7.6: so too, if, while he is giving attention to settling …
mn20:7.9: With the abandoning of them his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated.
mn20:8.1: ‘Bhikkhus, as soon as, after evil unprofitable thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion have arisen in a bhikkhu owing to some sign to which sign he was giving attention, any [such] evil unprofitable thoughts are abandoned in him and subside, when he gives attention to a sign other than that and connected with what is profitable,
mn20:8.2: and so his mind is settled in himself, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated—
mn20:8.3: and [as soon as] any [further] evil unprofitable thoughts ... are abandoned in him and subside when he scrutinizes the danger in those thoughts,
mn20:8.4: and so with the abandoning of them his mind is settled, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated—
mn20:8.5: and [as soon as] any [further] evil unprofitable thoughts ... are abandoned in him and subside when he tries forgetting these thoughts and non-attention to them,
mn20:8.6: and so his mind is settled, brought to singleness and concentrated—
mn20:8.7: and [as soon as] any [further] evil unprofitable thoughts ... are abandoned in him and subside when he gives attention to the settling of thought-formations with respect to those thoughts,
mn20:8.8: and so with the abandoning of them his mind is settled, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated—
mn20:8.9: and [as soon as] any [further] evil unprofitable thoughts ... are abandoned in him and subside when, with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth, he beats down, constrains and crushes mind with mind,
mn20:8.10: and so with the abandoning of them his mind is settled, quieted, brought to singleness and concentrated,
mn20:8.11: then that bhikkhu is called a master of the courses of thought processes,
mn20:8.12: he will think the thoughts that he wishes, and he will not think the thoughts that he does not wish.
mn20:8.13: He has severed craving, flung off the fetters, and rightly made an end of suffering with the penetration of conceit.’
mn20:8.14: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn20:8.15: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
